leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 files prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene with the same three laureates (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer), and all six describe it as a prediction (flat bands at a magic angle, 2011) followed by an experimental discovery (correlated insulating and superconducting states, 2018). Three of the six (Eriksson, Johansson, Pearce) moved to it from a different first choice in their opening ranking. What is shared: the laureate set, the theory-plus-experiment structure, and the view that the citation should rest on the prediction and the observed states and not on a settled pairing mechanism. What is not shared: how much weight the field's age (about eight years) and the open mechanism carry, and how to treat omitted credit (Yuan Cao, Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, other moire groups). Citation wordings differ slightly: Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson stay close to prediction plus discovery, while Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce add that it opened the field of moire quantum materials.

Two members prefer optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye, on the grounds of two-name attribution, independent confirmation at the 1e-18 level, more than two decades of maturity, and tests of relativity and constants with a possible redefinition of the second. They explicitly name B038 as their first (Kroll) or strongest (Lindroth) alternative, so the disagreement is about which criterion should weigh more, breadth of a new field versus completeness and cleanliness of a measurement advance, and not about the science of either. Their citations differ in emphasis (Kroll: invention and realisation of lattice clocks; Lindroth: from the magic-wavelength concept to uncertainties near one part in 10^18). Kroll also discloses a past link to the JILA-adjacent Hall environment, so the two supporters are not equivalent on conflict status.

areas_of_agreement: All eight files name B038 as either the preferred configuration or a named alternative (B038 is preferred by six, and is the first alternative of Kroll and Lindroth), and none disputes the core experimental observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states or its reproduction by independent groups.

B045 is named as a preferred configuration or as an alternative by all eight files (Kroll and Lindroth prefer it; Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce list it as an alternative), and its two-name credit and maturity are generally accepted, including by members who prefer B038.
For B038, members across the preference split want a citation that credits the 2011 prediction and the 2018 discovery without claiming an explanation of the superconducting pairing mechanism.
No file prefers more than one candidate; every file proposes a single prize part, and none proposes combining B038 and B045.

Members agree that the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits creates a timing issue for circuit QED (B026), including Johansson, who prefers B026 as an alternative but has reduced its weight.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus invention: Kroll and Lindroth argue that lattice clocks are a physical test and a new measurement regime, while Danielsson, Johansson and Olsson regard them as closer to a precision instrument. Olsson asks what new physics, as opposed to new accuracy, the clocks have revealed.

Novelty relative to earlier metrology prizes: the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion control prizes are cited as reasons for caution on B045; Kroll and Lindroth respond that the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct achievement, and Kroll adds that ion clocks reach similar uncertainties, so the citation should say what is specific to lattices.

Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder in B038 make the discovery secure but the field early (Mehlig, Olsson, Danielsson), or make quantitative comparison between laboratories weaker than for clocks (Lindroth, Kroll).
Whether DMFT (B037) counts as a discovery or a method; Eriksson moved it to an alternative, and Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce question it as a method with a weaker discovery element.
Whether IceCube (B016) should rest on the diffuse-flux detection or on source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068), which the files describe as still modest in significance.
attribution_disputes: B038: the three names are shared by all proposals, but Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 papers, earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and other moire groups are outside the credited set. Pearce and Mehlig argue the Bistritzer-MacDonald paper is the decisive prediction; Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson regard the allocation as defensible but contested. Several files rely on recalled priority history, not a checked source.

B045: Katori and Ye is the cleanest credit on the shortlist per Kroll, Lindroth and others, but Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow, Hinkley, other lattice-clock groups and single-ion clock groups are not credited, and neither supporter has verified the priority details.

B016: Halzen and Karle for a collaboration of hundreds leaves AMANDA leadership and other IceCube figures unexplained (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Danielsson); Pearce acknowledges that individual roles are partly collective.

B023 versus B040: both cover topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect with different credited sets (Kane, Molenkamp, Xue in B023; Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan in B040), so they are competing packagings of one field. Mehlig, Olsson, Eriksson and Pearce note that Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan cannot all be accommodated.
B037: Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce note that Metzner, who introduced the infinite-dimension limit with Vollhardt, is outside the credited names.
B026: Girvin is outside the credited trio (Johansson, Kroll, Olsson, Pearce note this).
maturity_disputes: B038 is about eight years old with an unresolved pairing mechanism; Mehlig, Danielsson and Eriksson say recognition need not wait for the mechanism, while Lindroth and Kroll weigh the age of the field and the open questions against it, and Olsson calls the argument that it may be slightly early the one taken most seriously. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce each record a version of this worry in their own case against.

B045 has more than two decades of independent confirmation, but the redefinition of the second has not happened, and Olsson and Pearce say timeliness should not rest on an event that has not occurred.
B016 has an established diffuse flux but source identification of the bulk of it remains limited, so it is placed as a strong alternative or later-year candidate by Danielsson and others.
Topological insulators (B023, B040) are described as mature and overdue by Mehlig but weakened by the 2016 topological-phases prize and by the attribution problem.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Pearce (chair) is an astroparticle experimentalist on PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and discloses that he would recuse from a final decision on B016 (IceCube) if it came to a vote, though no direct link to IceCube or its credited individuals is documented. He records no specific conflict for B038 or B045.

Johansson discloses a possible recusal issue on B026 (circuit QED) and to a lesser degree B007: work in superconducting circuit and waveguide QED, direction of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology at Chalmers, Chalmers colleagues and collaborators in the area, and Chalmers hosting researchers associated with the 2025 prize. Johansson has reduced the weight of the B026 first-place ranking. No conflict is recorded for B038 or B045.

Kroll discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory and notes that Ye's work is closely tied to Hall's group at JILA, so recusal or at least disclosure may apply to B045; no direct collaboration with Katori or Ye is documented. Kroll also notes proximity to atomic-physics candidates B007, B028 and B018.

Eriksson notes methodological proximity between B037 (DMFT) and own research on DFT and correlated-electron methods, and would flag it and could defer if B037 is taken up; no conflict is recorded for B038.
Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson record no specific conflict from their profiles. Lindroth notes adjacent expertise in relativistic atomic structure for B045 as background only.
questions_for_round2: B038 versus B045: should the committee weigh a new field of physics opened by a prediction confirmed by experiment more heavily than a mature, cleanly attributed measurement advance, and can Kroll and Lindroth say what new physics (not only new accuracy) lattice clocks have revealed, and can Mehlig, Olsson and the B038 supporters say whether their support would change if the pairing mechanism turned out to be conventional?

For B038, does the committee accept a citation anchored on the 2011 flat-band prediction and the 2018 observation of correlated and superconducting states, with no mechanism claimed, and does it accept the three-name set despite the omission of Yuan Cao and the earlier twisted-bilayer theorists, or does the age of the field and the unresolved mechanism argue for waiting?

For B045, should a citation say what is specific to lattice clocks as distinct from single-ion optical clocks and the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and does the committee treat the prospective redefinition of the second as relevant evidence of merit or as a future event?

If the committee wants a candidate other than B038 or B045 this year, which of B016, B026, B007 or the topological-insulator entries is the strongest fallback, given the IceCube credit question (diffuse flux versus source associations, and the two-name limit for a large collaboration), the 2025 overlap and Girvin omission for B026, and the competing credited sets in B023 and B040?

What should happen with members who have disclosed possible conflicts (Pearce on B016, Johansson on B026 and B007, Kroll on B045, Eriksson on B037): should they speak, recuse from the final ballot, or have their weight adjusted on those candidates, and does that change the count of explicit supporters in any configuration?
summary.chair_observation: The eight files split into a six-member group preferring B038 with an identical three-name set and a two-member group preferring B045 with an identical two-name set, and the B045 supporters name B038 as their strongest alternative. The remaining open points are mostly about weighting, namely field age and mechanism versus maturity and discovery versus invention, and about wording the citation. Several scientific and attribution claims, including the priority history of twisted-bilayer theory and the lattice-clock groups, rest on recollection and have not been checked against sources, so round 2 should say which claims are verified and which are assumed.
